request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Pallas by TxPipe: Maintaining Cardano's Core Rust Libraries, Year 2.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve and a 15,750 ADA Intersect administration fee, totaling 540,750 ADA.

Pallas is a collection of Rust crates implementing core Ouroboros and Cardano primitives including CBOR encoding, cryptography, networking, ledger traversal, transaction building, and address handling.
Pallas is used as shared infrastructure by projects including Aiken, Dolos, Lucid, Oura, Mithril, Amaru, UTxO-RPC, and others.
The document states Pallas has over 649 pull requests, 199 stars, 91 forks, 60 contributors, and 214,446 crates.io downloads, with links to GitHub and crates.io for verification.
The maintainer scope covers maintenance, community support, and AI-friendly documentation and integration resources.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold in the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission.
The proposer states the withdrawal does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the time of submission.
TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals from Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule.

Intersect will administer the funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with TRSC and PSSC addresses, multi-party authorization rules, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard.
The on-chain metadata lists a treasury withdrawal reward of 540,750,000,000 lovelace to the 2026 Treasury Reserve Smart Contract stake address.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for a 12-month Pallas maintenance grant administered by Intersect through treasury smart contracts, citing Pallas ecosystem usage, public repository metrics, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, prior TxPipe delivery history, and oversight arrangements.
